Fem.name: The Bias Cut
Fem.description: Dresses became more slim creating a slender, silhouette look. Dresses had elongated torsos with widening shoulders and flared out slightly at the ankle

Masc.name: More Formal Styles
Masc.description: Silhouettes slimmed down after the looser, baggy fits of the 1920s. Suits were worn with semi-accentuated waists to match the womenswear shift. New material such as sharkskin, a synthetic fabric, gained in popularity for suits

Fem.name: Era of Utility
Fem.description: WWII forced women's fashion to become highly practical, yet it retained a sharp elegance. The standard look was military-inspired toughness. Women entered the workforce and began wearing high-waisted, wide-leg trousers and denim overalls.

Masc.name: The Zoot Suit
Masc.description: The zoot suit was billowed with excess fabric. The suit style became popular with Black, Mexican American, and Latino men who found tailors to take in oversized suits

Fem.name: The New Look
Fem.description: Fashion embraced a feminine silhouettes with cinched waists, full skirts, gloves, and elegant dresses. Inspired by Hollywood glamour, women wore poodle skirts, sweater sets, and fitted tops.

Masc.name: Era of Rock and Roll
Masc.description: Men's fashion mixed formal wear with rebellious youth culture. Leather jackets, white t-shirts, cuffed jeans, and slicked-back hair became iconic thanks to rock and roll culture.

Fem.name: Mod Fashion
Fem.description: The 1960s introduced bold colors, geometric prints, and the miniskirt. Fashion became youthful and experimental with go-go boots, shift dresses, and sleek hairstyles.

Masc.name: The Mod Look
Masc.description: Slim-cut suits, turtlenecks, Chelsea boots, and mop-top hairstyles defined menswear. British bands heavily influenced style, creating a clean and modern aesthetic.

Fem.name: Bohemian Glam
Fem.description: Women embraced bell-bottom jeans, platform shoes, fringe jackets, and earthy colors. Disco fashion later introduced sequins, jumpsuits, and glittering fabrics.

Masc.name: Disco Fever
Masc.description: Menswear became expressive with flared pants, colorful suits, patterned shirts, and platform shoes. Long hair and wide collars completed the bold disco-inspired look.

Fem.name: Power Dressing
Fem.description: Fashion became loud and confident with neon colors, oversized blazers, shoulder pads, leggings, and teased hair. Athletic wear and glam styles both dominated the decade.

Masc.name: Bold Excess
Masc.description: Men wore acid-wash jeans, leather jackets, tracksuits, and oversized clothing. Bright colors, mullets, and athletic-inspired streetwear became mainstream.

Fem.name: Minimalist Grunge
Fem.description: Fashion shifted toward relaxed and casual styles with slip dresses, flannel shirts, chokers, ripped jeans, and combat boots. Minimalism mixed with alternative fashion became popular.

Masc.name: Streetwear Rise
Masc.description: Baggy jeans, oversized t-shirts, sneakers, and flannel shirts defined the decade. Hip-hop and grunge culture heavily influenced everyday menswear.

Fem.name: Y2K Fashion
Fem.description: Low-rise jeans, crop tops, rhinestones, velour tracksuits, and shiny metallic fabrics captured the futuristic Y2K aesthetic. Pop stars heavily influenced trends. The digital age inspired this too.

Masc.name: Baggy Street Style
Masc.description: Cargo pants, oversized jerseys, graphic tees, and layered outfits became popular. Skater culture, hip-hop, and sporty fashion shaped the early 2000s look.

Fem.name: Social Media Fashion
Fem.description: This era introduced aesthetics with influencer culture. Skater skirts, leggings, and oversized sweaters. Galaxy print was also big on leggings and backpacks.

Masc.name: Athleisure Style
Masc.description: Skinny jeans, baggy jeans, sneakers, hoodies, joggers, and streetwear brands became dominant. Sportswear also became popular.
